tests: Before my work: `tests/acceptance/W2-49` 129 passed. After, the same command (`PYTHONPATH=…/W2-49-tests/src TMPDIR=<sandbox tmp> python3 -m pytest tests/acceptance/W2-49 -q -p no:cacheprovider -rs`): **10 failed, 144 passed**, so all 129 earlier tests are green. Behaviour by behaviour:
(1) Line 3, `test_validator_passes_both_cit_p_checks_on_this_tree`: GREEN. On this tree the validator prints `PASS cit-p-moved-items — 3 items moved to Wave 2, each with a CIT-P line` and `PASS cit-p-lines-applied — 6 CIT-P lines, each applied in the Contract`. It is green because W2-51's validator, v4.2 and the CIT-P's §6.1 lines are all in this tree.
(2) The failure line, all GREEN, all on a temporary tree of the single files the two checks read (the WBS, `contract.yaml`, the five `*-CIT-P.md` files):
- a control test: that tree, unchanged, passes both checks;
- `…moved_to_wave_2_without_its_cit_p_line_fails_naming_it[CAP-44.f, CAP-44.h, CAP-43.b]`;
- `…cit_p_line_with_no_change_in_the_contract_fails_naming_it[CAP-43.b, CAP-43.d, CAP-44.f, CAP-44.h, CAP-44.k, CAP-44.l]`;
- `…cit_p_line_for_an_item_the_contract_does_not_change_fails_naming_it` (an extra line, CAP-45.a in W3).
Each case makes one change, and only the named check fails, naming only that id. That is how the tests show the three moved items and six lines are covered, rather than by asserting counts. They are green because the behaviour holds: on stand-ins, a validator that always prints PASS fails all 10 failure cases; one whose FAIL reasons name no id fails the same 10; a CIT-P with CAP-44.h's line removed fails line 3 and the control.
(3) Source map: `…row_states_its_part_lite_in_wave_2_and_the_rest_in_wave_3[8 rows]` is RED (8). The message is `<doc> / <item> does not state its part as Wave 2, lite, under CAP-44.f (Contract v4.2): '<cell as before>'`, with CAP-44.h for the two verdict rows. The A11 ("16. G") and A9 ("Stage A9") rows test (2) and `…no_row_but_the_eight_differs_from_before_this_ticket` (1) are GREEN now because the file is unchanged since `ffc60703e373`; they guard the change.
(4) Records: `test_cap_45a_record_carries_contract_v4_2_item_text` is RED (`title 'gov update: check/impact, authenticated source (signed tag), …' is not contract.yaml's item`). `test_every_capability_record_states_the_contracts_status` is RED (`276 of 276 capability records do not state the Contract's status ACCEPTED`).
Stand-in checks (outside the tree, single named files): two passing stand-ins with the decided behaviour, in two wordings of the eight rows, pass 25/25. Each break failed with its stated message:
- source map: Stage A7 left as it was; CAP-44.f given W3 and no W2; no CAP-44.k part; a verdict row under the wrong ids; the A9 row changed; an unrelated row changed; one of the eight with its `class` changed; a row with five columns;
- records: CAP-45.a's record stale; its heading alone stale; one record still PROPOSED;
- validator: the three breaks above.
discoveries: (a) The validator counts every file under `tests/acceptance/` as citing any Contract id it contains (W2-51's reading R4). If a test file names DEC-841's nine items, the `contract-items-cited-by-tests` check changes, so no file in this suite names them; that check's output is the same before and after my commit. (b) The validator's PASS reasons give only counts, in wording no test fixes. So the coverage is shown by single-change cases, and no count is asserted, which also keeps the tests independent of DEC-841. (c) The existing K (2) test compares a record's `status` with its sibling's, so setting every record to ACCEPTED contradicts no earlier test.
risks: (a) The rule for what a source-map row "states" is my own assumption, not a source; it is written in the README. A cell is split at `;` and `. ` outside brackets; one part must name the lite id with "lite" and W2, and one must name the rest's id with W3. A part naming both items and both waves passes. (b) The "no other row" test compares rows in order, so a re-sorted file would fail it. (c) Line 3 runs on the whole tree, so a later CIT-P from another ticket that breaks either check would turn it red.
lessons: Never name DEC-841's nine ids in any file under `tests/acceptance/`. Pull a ticket's facts out of the validator by changing one thing per case, not by its wording. Single named files are enough for stand-ins; `git show` of a fixed commit works from a stand-in when `GIT_DIR` points at the repository's git folder.
